summary: Online lending and interest-account platform that pooled customer funds, stopped deposits and withdrawals in November 2022, moved toward an orderly liquidation, and later became the subject of California and SEC enforcement findings concerning unlicensed products, misrepresentations, misuse of investor funds, and TerraUSD losses.
what_happened: MyConstant offered a loan-matching service, crypto interest accounts, and fiat interest accounts. California regulators found that the company offered unlicensed loan-brokering and unqualified securities products. The SEC later found that the founder misrepresented the loan strategy, misappropriated part of investor funds, and used at least $11.9 million to purchase TerraUSD, producing major losses after UST collapsed. MyConstant ceased operations and customer withdrawals on 17 November 2022, announced an orderly liquidation, and entered customer litigation and settlement proceedings.
uncertainty_notes: The May 2019 launch date represents the approximate start of the Loan Matching Service identified by the SEC. Customer recoveries span prior private plan payments, a proposed class-settlement liquidating trust, and possible SEC distributions; no single final recovery percentage should be inferred. A currently resolving domain does not establish that the original lending service resumed operations.
notes: Added as a major centralized lending and yield failure with state and federal regulatory findings and an ongoing customer-recovery process.
